findings.obs_text: In Jer 23:27 the prophets think to make the people forget the Lord's name by their dreams: the thought is a plan aimed at forgetting. In 2Pe 1:13 Peter thinks it right to stir them up by reminder: the judgment serves remembering.
findings.grounds: who think to make my people forget my name

findings.obs_text: In Isa 55:7 the unrighteous man who forsakes his thoughts and returns is promised abundant pardon: forsaking the thoughts is joined to God's pardon.
In Isa 55:7 the unrighteous man is to forsake his thoughts: the thoughts are what is to be left. In 1Ch 28:9 the Lord, who understands every plan and thought, will cast off the one who forsakes him.
findings.grounds: if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever

findings.obs_text: In Mat 5:17 the hearers are not to think Jesus came to abolish the Law: the false thought is corrected by his coming to fulfill it.
findings.grounds: I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them

findings.obs_text: In Joh 11:56 the people ask one another what they think, whether Jesus will come to the feast, and in Joh 13:29 some think Jesus sent Judas to buy for the feast: the feast is the setting of a view about Jesus, mistaken in Joh 13:29.
findings.grounds: Buy what we need for the feast

findings.obs_text: In Phili 1:17 some proclaim Christ from selfish ambition, thinking to afflict Paul in prison: the intent to harm goes with the selfish motive.
findings.grounds: thinking to afflict me in my imprisonment

findings.obs_text: In 2Ki 20:19 and Isa 39:8 Hezekiah thinks there will be peace and security in his days: the thought rests on his own safety. In 2Ch 32:1 Sennacherib besieges the walled towns, meaning to take them. In Jer 40:5 the captain of the guard leaves Jeremiah to go where he thinks right.
findings.grounds: There will be peace and security in my days

findings.obs_text: In Mat 6:7 the Gentiles expect a hearing because they pile up words: a false view of prayer. In Luk 8:18 the hearers are to take care how they hear, for what one thinks he has may be taken. In Job 32:10 Elihu asks to be heard as he gives his opinion, and in 2Cor 12:6 Paul wants no one to think more of him than what is heard from him.
findings.grounds: they think that they will be heard for their many words
